Name: Dragon's Back (Shek O Country Park)
Location: Trailhead at To Tei Wan on Shek O Road, Shek O Country Park, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: A well-signposted ridge walk of roughly 7.5 km with sea views over Tai Long Wan, Shek O and Stanley, ending at Big Wave Bay or Shek O village. Why: The classic easy-to-reach HK Island hike: MTR to beach in a half day, with a swim-free coast ending at Shek O's cafes. Best for first-time hikers and photographers wanting ridge-line sea views.

Name: Lion Rock and Amah Rock (Lion Rock Country Park)
Location: Lion Rock Country Park, Kowloon (common starts: Wong Tai Sin or Lok Fu, Amah Rock via Hung Mui Kuk), Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: The peak that looms over Kowloon and gives Hong Kongers their 'Lion Rock spirit'. Common routes are about 5 km from Lok Fu to Wong Tai Sin, with a short 15-minute detour to Amah Rock from the Hung Mui Kuk barbecue area. Why: The cultural symbol of the city, with a view straight down on the estates and across the harbour. Rewarding for photography at golden hour but the summit route has a steep exposed scramble.

Name: Lantau Peak via Lantau Trail Section 3
Location: Pak Kung Au to Ngong Ping, Lantau Island, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: The official 4.5 km, about 2.5 h section climbs Hong Kong's second-highest peak (about 934 m) by a steep staircase, ending at Ngong Ping near the Big Buddha. Why: Sunrise hike of choice and a finish at the Big Buddha and Po Lin Monastery; it combines mountain and temple in one trip. For fit hikers; the steep ladder section is the crux.

Name: Sunset Peak (Lantau Trail Section 2)
Location: Nam Shan to Pak Kung Au, Lantau Island, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Lantau Trail Section 2: about 6.5 km and 3.5 h with the climb to Sunset Peak (Tai Tung Shan), Hong Kong's third highest peak, with wide views of the island and out to sea. Why: Named for its sunsets; a good alternative to the busier Lantau Peak, with grassy open ridges. Hikers in the know stay for the city lights, so bring a torch.

Name: Sai Wan and Tai Long Wan beaches (MacLehose Trail Section 2)
Location: Sai Wan Pavilion terminus (Sai Kung East Country Park); also via High Island Reservoir East Dam, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Remote white-sand beaches in Sai Kung East Country Park reached on foot. Easiest route is from Sai Wan Pavilion by about an hour's walk; longer routes start from the East Dam (about 6.6 km, 2 to 2.5 h to Sai Wan). Why: Often called the best beaches in Hong Kong; a classic winter day hike with sea views that feels far from the city. Strong rip currents and no lifeguards, so look not swim.

Name: High Island Geo Trail (East Dam)
Location: High Island Reservoir East Dam, Sai Kung East Country Park, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Easy flat walk beside the East Dam where hexagonal volcanic rock columns (about 140 million years old) and tetrapod breakwaters line the shore, part of the Hong Kong UNESCO Global Geopark. Why: Hong Kong's most dramatic geology with minimal effort; the columns are at Po Pin Chau by boat or the East Dam walk. Travellers who like geology and photography.

Name: Pat Sin Leng Nature Trail
Location: Pat Sin Leng Country Park, Tai Po / Fanling, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Official nature trail of 4 km and 2 h, rated moderate, with steep stone steps on a ridge of eight peaks overlooking Plover Cove and Starling Inlet. Why: One of Hong Kong's most scenic ridgelines and less tourist-heavy; top choice for northern NT views in clear winter weather. Pairs with Plover Cove and Bride's Pool.

Name: Plover Cove Reservoir and Tai Mei Tuk
Location: Tai Mei Tuk, Plover Cove Country Park, Tai Po, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: A flat reservoir dam with water views, a cycle track along Tolo Harbour and the Bride's Pool waterfall nearby, forming an easy day out from Tai Po. Why: A relaxed non-summit option; rent a bike at Tai Mei Tuk or walk the dam. Good for families and anyone avoiding steep climbs.

Name: Peak Circle Walk (Lugard Road and Harlech Road)
Location: Lugard Road, The Peak (starts near Peak Tower), Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: A mostly flat loop of about 3.5 km (1-1.5 h) with Lugard Road's cliffside views over the harbour and Harlech Road shaded by trees and a small waterfall. Why: Free alternative to paying for the Sky Terrace, with the best harbour views and an easy walk. Suitable for anyone with children or limited fitness.

Name: Tai Mo Shan (957 m)
Location: Tai Mo Shan Visitor Centre, Route Twisk, Tsuen Kam Au, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Hong Kong's highest peak; the popular route runs from the visitor centre up Tai Mo Shan Road to the weather station. Why: Winter sea-of-cloud views; easier route is relatively gentle.

Name: Hong Kong Wetland Park
Location: Wetland Park Road, Tin Shui Wai, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Visitor centre and wetland reserve. Why: Winter bird season; open on public holidays.

Name: Tung Ping Chau
Location: Ma Liu Shui Ferry Pier, Science Park Road, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Remote Geopark island reached by ferry from Ma Liu Shui; weekend and public-holiday service only. Why: Ferry runs only weekends and holidays; Sunday 09:00 out, 17:15 back (Transport Department listing, undated).

Name: Sharp Peak (Nam She Tsim)
Location: Trail start at Pak Tam Au, Sai Kung East Country Park (bus stop on Sai Kung Road toward Wong Shek), Sai Kung, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: A jagged 468 m pyramid-shaped peak on the Sai Kung peninsula with 360-degree views over Tai Long Wan, the High Island Reservoir and Port Shelter. The final approach is a steep scramble on loose sandy ground. Why: Often called Hong Kong's most spectacular and most dangerous day hike; a bucket-list climb for experienced hikers and the signature Sai Kung summit.

Name: High West (Victoria Peak western summit)
Location: Trail from Lugard Road / Peak Road, The Peak, Hong Kong (Hong Kong Trail Section 1 toward Pok Fu Lam Reservoir), Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: A short, scenic route to the 494 m western summit above Victoria Peak, with open views over Lamma, Cheung Chau and the western harbour. It links to Hong Kong Trail Section 1 (about 7 km, 2 h) down to Pok Fu Lam Reservoir. Why: A quick way to leave the Peak Tower crowds behind and get a summit view; combines naturally with the Lugard Road lookout loop.

Name: Devil's Peak (Lei Yue Mun)
Location: Trail from Yau Tong MTR Exit A via Ko Chiu Road and Lei Yue Mun Estate, Yau Tong, Kowloon, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: A short, partly paved climb up Devil's Peak with views over Lei Yue Mun channel, Victoria Harbour and Tseung Kwan O, past WWII Gough Battery and Fort remains, ending in Lei Yue Mun village. Why: An easy WWII-history hike with excellent harbour-mouth views that finishes at Lei Yue Mun's seafood restaurants for a combined hike-and-seafood day.

Name: Violet Hill and The Twins (Wilson Trail Stage 1)
Location: Trailhead at Wong Nai Chung Reservoir Park, Wong Nai Chung Gap Road, Happy Valley, Hong Kong; ends at Stanley Gap Road, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: A ridge walk from Wong Nai Chung Reservoir over Violet Hill and the Twins (Stanley's twin peaks) to Stanley Gap Road, with views of Repulse Bay, Stanley and Tai Tam. About 4.8 km with steep stair sections. Why: The classic 'twin peaks' hike on Hong Kong Island and the quickest way to arrive in Stanley on foot, with a shoreline finish.

Name: Jardine's Lookout
Location: Trailhead on Tai Tam Reservoir Road near Wong Nai Chung Gap, Tai Hang / Happy Valley, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: A compact hike to a 433 m summit with one of the best skyline and harbour views on the island, looking over Causeway Bay, Victoria Harbour and Kowloon, with Tai Tam reservoirs behind. Can be extended to Mount Butler or Siu Ma Shan. Why: A near-the-city viewpoint that gives a Peak-like vista without the crowds, good for golden hour and blue hour.

Name: Tai Tam Reservoirs and Hong Kong Trail Section 6
Location: Tai Tam Country Park, Tai Tam Reservoir Road / Tai Tam Reservoir North stop, Tai Tam, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: A gentle walk along Hong Kong Island's largest reservoir group, with Edwardian waterworks including the arched Tai Tam Reservoir Bridges, aqueducts and valve houses; Hong Kong Trail Section 6 links Mount Parker Road to Tai Tam Road. Why: An easy, family-friendly heritage walk through colonial waterworks, with shaded forest and reservoir views just minutes from the city.

Name: Ng Tung Chai Waterfalls
Location: Ng Tung Chai village (bus/minibus terminus), Tai Mo Shan Country Park, Tai Po, New Territories, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: A forested stream valley below Tai Mo Shan with four main waterfalls (Bottom Fall, Main Fall, Scattered Fall, Cascades, Yuk Nui) reached by a stepped path through a traditional Hakka village. Why: Hong Kong's best-known waterfall hike, with a rural village-to-forest feel; in dry December the falls are smaller but the trail is less muddy and quiet on weekdays.

Name: Ma On Shan ridge
Location: Ma On Shan Country Park (start near Ma On Shan MTR station / Heng On Estate), Sha Tin, New Territories, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: A steep ridge scramble to the 702 m summit of Ma On Shan (Horse Saddle Mountain) with sweeping views to Sai Kung, Sha Tin and Tolo Harbour; exposed, hands-on sections near the top. Why: One of the toughest, most dramatic ridge walks in the territory, reachable by MTR with no car.
